question: [PRACTICE] What will the average "new forecasters per day" be on this question before this question closes?

calls.reasoning: Resolves as (unique forecasters shown at close) / (days open), tenth-rounded. Numerator is directly observed and still climbing: 128 on 2026-09-13 (scaffold trace) -> 135 on 2026-09-15 (live page), ~3.2/day; the page's '1.1 forecasters this week' is the aggregate's movement in question units, NOT inflow, so the counter is not saturated. Projecting 12.3 remaining days with mild decay plus the pre-season onboarding surge seen in the Summer analog (bot activity clustered the day before that season started) gives F ~152-205, median ~170. Denominator is the crux and is not published: post-ID adjacency dates creation to ~Sep 5-6 (45516 sits 2 IDs below the MiniBench batch 45518-45577 that my bot began sweeping 2026-09-07T00:36Z, while batch 45286-45326 was swept Aug 24-25), and the adjacent bot-testing twin 45517 closes Sep 5, 2028 - a 2-year window from a Sep 5, 2026 creation. So D ~21-24, median ~22.5, and D cannot exceed ~24 unless that dating is wrong. 170/22.5 = 7.6; I shade to 7.3 and keep a fat left tail because the on-page bot aggregate (5.55, up from ~4.4 a week ago) sits well below me - explicable by the misread activity line pinning others' numerator near 130 and by a lagging recency-weighted mix, but I may simply be wrong about the open date. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker contract on this or any Metaculus-participation metric - none found; the harness title search also returned nothing. Escape: >10.05 needs F>220 at D=22 (~7/day sustained, 40% above the Summer analog's total) - priced at 3%; <0.95 would need D>180 days, arithmetically impossible, so no lower escape declared.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the FORECASTER count displayed in the Metaculus UI for this post (post 45516, question 45707, slug 'average-forecasters-for-fall-futureeval') on its close date, divided by the number of days the question was open; rounded to the nearest tenth. It does NOT resolve off number of predictions submitted (a bot re-forecasting adds nothing), off comments, off tournament registrations, or off any tournament-wide statistic.

EVENT WINDOW: per the criteria, this question's own open date -> close 2026-09-28T07:00:00Z (the scaffold's API-derived record carries close_time 2026-09-28T05:59:00Z). The open timestamp is NOT published on any anonymous surface: the Metaculus API returns 403 ('only available to authenticated users'), the rendered page contains no 'opened'/'published' string, and the Wayback Machine has no snapshot of the page. It must be inferred (evidence below). If the open date is 2026-09-05, then as of Now (2026-09-15T23:20Z) about 47% of the window has elapsed and 12.3 days remain; if 2026-09-06, about 45%; if 2026-08-28, about 60%.

OBSERVED STATE (time series, both readings of the same UI field):
- 2026-09-13T22:40Z: 128 forecasters, 0 comments (recorded by this scaffold's own trace, three independent fetches agreeing).
- 2026-09-15T~23:00Z: 135 forecasters, 0 comments, 'Closes Sep 28, 2026', tournament label 'Fall 2026 FutureEval Bot Tournament' (live page via text-extraction proxy).
- That is +7 forecasters in ~2.2 days.
- CAUTION ON A MISREADABLE FIELD: the page also shows a line reading '1.1 forecasters this week' (it read '1 forecasters this week' on Sep 13). Because this question's UNIT is 'forecasters', this line is the community estimate's weekly MOVEMENT expressed in question units - it is not a count of new forecasters. Reading it as inflow implies a saturated counter, which the 128->135 series directly contradicts.

DATING THE OPEN (evidence, both directions):
- Metaculus post IDs are allocated monotonically at creation; a post cannot open before it is created. This scaffold's forecast journal gives an ID->date map from the dates it first forecast each post: posts 45286-45326 were swept 2026-08-24/25 (a Monday MiniBench batch), and posts 45518-45577 (~60 consecutive IDs, the next biweekly Monday batch) were swept starting 2026-09-07T00:36Z. Post 45516 sits 2 IDs below that batch, i.e. created immediately before it; at the ~15 IDs/day implied between the two batches, that is hours, not days, before the batch.
- Corroboration: the adjacent twin post 45517 (same title, permanent 'Bot testing area', 35 forecasters) shows 'Closes Sep 5, 2028' - a 2-year window pointing at a 2026-09-05 creation/open.
- Pointing EARLIER (longer window): Fall 2026 season questions were already live and resolving in late August 2026 (a Fall-feed question resolved Aug 31), so the season's flow predates September; and the Summer precedent had practice material available ~2-3 weeks before the season start.
- Pointing LATER (shorter window): the MiniBench batch adjacent in ID space did not open until ~Sep 7 00:00Z; this scaffold, which polls the tournament feed, first forecast post 45516 on 2026-09-09 despite forecasting the 45518+ batch from Sep 7.

BASE RATES / COUNTS, WITH THE CLASS EACH IS COMPUTED OVER:
- Over FutureEval pre-season [PRACTICE] warm-up questions attached to a seasonal tournament (n=1 directly observed): Summer 2026 post 43339 closed with 156 forecasters and 342 comments. Its window is not published; the adjacent-ID Summer announcement notebook 43340 was published 2026-05-01 and the Summer season started 2026-05-18, which if the practice question opened with the announcement implies a ~17-day window (156/17 = 9.2 per day); a window of 23 days instead implies 6.8 per day.
- Over the SAME question text but conditioned on the permanent unscored bot-testing venue rather than a seasonal tournament: twin post 45517 shows 35 forecasters against a multi-year window - a far thinner venue.
- Over regular scored questions in the Summer 2026 season (sampled resolved feed): forecaster counts 169, 137, 121, 104, 99, 98, 96, 93, 91, 88, 80, 39 - central tendency ~95-105, top decile ~165.
- Over tournament ROSTERS: Spring 2026 FutureEval had 173 bots (111 external + 65 in-house) and 10 pro forecasters across 297 scored questions. Each bot contributes at most one to a forecaster count, so the count is bounded by roster size plus new entrants.
- Over season structure: FutureEval seasons start every January, May and September; 300-500 questions; $50k pool; the Fall 2026 season's own questions start opening 2026-09-28 - the same instant this question closes. MiniBench injects ~60 questions every other Monday (observed batches: Aug 24, Sep 7).

STRUCTURAL NOTES (carry both):
- Unique-forecaster counts front-load: a standing cron-driven bot roster sweeping a newly opened tournament question exhausts itself within days, after which a longer window raises the denominator faster than the numerator.
- Counter-pressure: the stated purpose of the question is warm-up for new entrants, and the Summer analog's page shows a mass of bot comments dated 2026-05-17, the day before that season started - i.e. late entrants arrive in the final days before a season opens, which for this question is inside the remaining window.
- The author set the range 0.95-10.05 (both bounds open, tenth rounding) while knowing the open and close dates exactly; only the forecaster count was uncertain to them.

calls.reasoning: Resolves off the forecaster count in the Metaculus UI on 2026-09-28 divided by days open, rounded to a tenth. Reference class: FutureEval seasonal warm-up questions, where the one documented analogue drew 156 forecasters and the prior season fielded 173 bots; over a nominal three-week warm-up that anchors ~7.4/day. I adjust down because this window is pre-season: the Fall main tournament only starts opening questions at the exact moment this closes, and the warm-up MiniBench opens Sept 21, so a large share of bot-makers deploy after or barely before this question's close, making N a fraction of the full-season population that accumulated the 156. I adjust the denominator toward 14 days: a bot-maker's Sept 14 issue about handling the newly-published pre-start Fall practice question implies a Sept 13-14 open against the Sept 28 07:00 close. Neither leg is confirmed - I could not read open_time or the live forecaster count (Metaculus API is auth-gated, site 403s), so this is inference from third-party traces, and I stay wide accordingly. Counter-case in both directions: if Metaculus's ~65 in-house Metac Bots fire on practice questions before the season, N clears 140 and the outcome escapes above 10.05 (priced at 9%); if the question actually opened in early September, D near 25 drags the ratio to ~4. No human market prices this.

BASE RATES (with the class each is computed over):
- Over FutureEval seasonal practice questions specifically: the Summer 2026 practice question (Major state exits EU before 2027) shows 156 forecasters. Its open and close dates are not stated in the accessible sources; its resolution subject runs to 2027, consistent with a long life rather than a two-week window. Computed per-day, this single case yields ~1.2/day if spread over a ~130-day season life, ~11.1/day if compressed into a 14-day window - the class supports both readings and the divisor is the unresolved variable.
- Over the full seasonal bot population (unconditional): 173 bots in Spring 2026 is the ceiling-ish figure for how many distinct forecasters a Fall tournament question could attract.
- Conditional on the window being PRE-start (before the season's first scored questions open): no published figure found for what fraction of the eventual population is deployed. Bot-maker behavior documented above (MiniBench on Sept 21, main start Sept 28) means some share of makers deploy only at or after this question's close.

STATUS QUO: the question is open and unresolved as of Now; forecaster counts on Metaculus are monotonically non-decreasing, accumulating fastest immediately after open (scheduled bots fire on their first run) and flattening afterward, so a longer open window mechanically lowers the ratio unless new entrants keep arriving.
